marketing_niche_leads.content:
If you're a roofer, a plumber, an attorney, or a dentist, here's a question most marketing agencies never ask you:

How much is one customer worth?

Not per visit. Over their lifetime.

If a roofing customer calls you for a repair, pays $800, and then calls you 3 years later for a full replacement at $15,000 : that customer is worth $15,800, not $800.

But most marketing is built around the $800 number.

That changes everything about the math.

If one customer is worth $15,800, you can afford to spend $1,580 to acquire them. That's a 10% CAC-to-LTV ratio.

But if you're only calculating based on the first $800 transaction, you think you can only afford $80.

And that's why you're bidding on cheap clicks that don't convert instead of investing in the trust, authority, and visibility that actually wins high-value customers.

The $20K Profit Gap Diagnostic looks at your true customer lifetime value ; not just the first transaction.

Half the time, the growth path isn't "get more leads."

It's "get the right leads and keep them longer."

Run the diagnostic. Find the real number.

→ https://lnkd.in/e9wZFRii

#LocalBusiness #ROIMath #BusinessGrowth #ProfitGap #LTV

marketing_niche_leads.content:
“A few years ago we were flying. I wish we’d invested in marketing then.”

That was something a founder said to me recently.

The market is harder for them now. More competitive. Harder to win new business.

They know they need marketing. 
They’re just not sure they can justify the cost when things are tighter.

Now of course, hindsight is 20/20.

It would have been easier to invest in marketing a few years ago when revenue was growing every month. 

But that's exactly why the investment is so important now.

Because the efforts of their sales teams isn't being multiplied effectively.

Marketing can be a growth lever when done right.

It’s how you can build something with value that lasts. 

Brand. Pipeline. A reputation that brings people to you. 
The justification for working retained only or holding firm on the margin.

Waiting for the perfect moment to start usually just means starting later than you should.

In-house marketer. Fractional CMO. Agency. 

However you do it, use marketing as a growth lever. Because it's not about whether you can afford marketing, it becomes whether you can afford not to.
